challenge.name: The Silent Store Gap
challenge.description: A batch of till scan lines from the northern stores was silently dropped during last night's ingestion, causing the model to forecast zero demand for fresh produce. #reliability_ruth# argues that the ingestion pipeline must be fully automated to guarantee every store's data arrives on time, while #data_dave# is willing to accept a manual verification step to ensure data quality before it reaches the feature store.

output.content: The northern stores incident exposed a critical gap in our monitoring. We need the ingestion pipeline to be fully automated with strict arrival guarantees. Every store scan line must land in the feature store before the nightly forecast job begins. The more reliable this process becomes, the fewer times we will run on incomplete data. I want to eliminate the manual handoffs that allow silent drops to slip through unnoticed. This is not about adding a single check; it is about building a system where data latency is impossible. The current setup leaves too much room for human error during the overnight window. We need a robust, automated flow that alerts us the moment a batch is missing, rather than waiting until the morning order window reveals the damage. Reliability is the foundation for everything else we build on top of this platform.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states that increasing the reliability of the ingestion pipeline will reduce the frequency of running on incomplete data, indicating that doing more to ensure this reliability would make them happier.
